meta.scope: Per-ISO input-referred read noise (electrons) and Photographic Dynamic Range (PDR, EV) for the three camera sensors picked in data/sensors.json, sourced from Bill Claff's photonstophotos.net. See research/read-noise.md for method, exact URLs and a per-camera prose table.
meta.method: photonstophotos.net's RN_e.htm and PDR.htm render their charts with Highcharts 4.0.4 from a `series` array written directly into an inline <script> tag on page load (not fetched from a separate JSON/XHR endpoint — there is no separate data file; the numbers are literal JS in the HTML). A plain text-only fetch that strips <script> content (as an earlier pass's WebFetch tool did) sees none of it. This pass used Playwright (headless Chromium, from this project's own node_modules) to load each page, then read the page's own HTML (which already contains the full, evaluated series array for every camera the site tracks) and parsed the `series: [ ... ]` array as JavaScript data with a bracket-balanced extraction + `new Function('return ' + text)()` (safe here: the extracted text is a plain data literal with marker objects only, no executable logic). This is a direct read of the exact numbers Highcharts plots, not a screen-read of chart pixels.
meta.isoConversion: Both charts place ISO on a log2 x-axis in 1/3-stop steps; the site's own xAxis label formatter is `ISO = round(3.125 * 2^x)`, applied here identically. RN_e.htm's y-axis is `log2(read noise in electrons)` (its own yAxis title says so); this file reports `readNoiseE = round(2^y, 3 decimals)`. PDR.htm's y-axis is PDR directly in EV, used as-is.
meta.markerSemantics: Per RN_e.htm's own on-page notes: an open/white-filled point marks a value outside the camera's 'normal analog range' (an extended low or high ISO reached by a digital push/pull rather than a real analog-gain step) — carried here as `outsideNormalAnalogRange: true`. A 'triangle-down' marker means in-camera noise reduction is being applied at that ISO; 'triangle-up' means additional digital scaling; both carried here as `digitalMarker`. Plain (un-marked) points are the vanilla, analog-gain-only measurements.
meta.dcgDetectionMethod: dcgIso is not published by the site as a single field on this chart; it is this session's read of the curve, found programmatically as the ISO step with the steepest negative slope in log2(read noise) vs log2(ISO) between two consecutive, unmarked, in-normal-range points (excluding the extended-ISO digital-pull region and the noise-reduction/scaling region at the top, which are not conversion-gain effects). The candidate is reported as the bracketing ISO pair (fromIso -> toIso), which is how Jim Kasson describes it too (e.g. 'the transition from ISO 250 to ISO 320'). This is a derived reading of Claff's own measured curve, not a number the site states directly in text.
meta.unityGainAndFwc: unityGainIso and fwcElectrons come from two independent places on the same site and are recorded separately, not averaged, when they differ: (1) each RN_e.htm series carries `unityEv`/`fwc` fields in its own Highcharts config (used to compute the chart's own legend-click tooltip, e.g. 'Unity ISO ...' and a per-ISO 'Saturation (e-)' column) -- this is Claff's own primary-chart data. (2) Sensor_Characteristics.htm ('DxOMark Derived Sensor Characteristics', a different, DxOMark-score-derived dataset Claff separately publishes) gives its own `unitygain`/`fwc`/`readnoise`/`isoinvariantat` per camera, recorded under `dxomarkDerived` where the camera appears in that table. The two datasets are close but not identical, as expected from two different derivations.
meta.evidenceKind: reported — all figures below are Bill Claff's own published measurements/derivations (photonstophotos.net), read directly from the chart's underlying data, not independently re-measured by this session.
openProblems: dcgIso is this session's own slope-based reading of the published curve, described above; it is not a value the site states as a single labeled number on these two charts, so treat it as `derived` from `reported` data, not itself `reported`.
Sensor_Characteristics.htm ('DxOMark Derived') has no OM-1 or E-M1 Mark III row -- DxOMark has not tested either camera -- so `dxomarkDerived` is only populated for the full-frame and APS-C picks.

The a7R IV's own RN_e.htm/PDR.htm/Sensor_Characteristics.htm series are all keyed 'Sony ILCE-7RM4', i.e. full-frame (36x24mm) readout; the same RN_e.htm page also carries a separate 'Sony ILCE-7RM4(APS-C)' series (the camera's in-camera APS-C crop mode), not used here since data/sensors.json's full-frame pick is the native full-frame mode.

photonstophotos.net's per-camera bit-depth suffix ('_12' vs '_14') on RN_e.htm reflects the raw file's bit depth for that model on that chart, not a claim this project makes about ADC bit depth; data/sensors.json's own adcBitDepthBits fields are the citations for that.

dxomarkDerived.note: Full well here (35,520 e-) is close to but not identical to the RN_e.htm chart's own fwc (34,452 e-) -- two different derivations of the same camera by the same site; recorded separately, not averaged. Both are well below the existing data/sensors.json in-camera figure (37,000 e-, Kasson blog) and further below the bare-chip ZWO ASI6200 figure (51,400 e-); all four numbers describe different measurement methods/contexts of what is very likely the same IMX455 silicon.

notes: DCG-switch candidate for the a6400 itself is ISO 318 -> 400 (essentially ISO 320 -> 400). This directly resolves the open conflict flagged in the existing research/sensor-sources.md ('the charts... indicate the dual gain ISO kicks in at ISO 400' vs 'an alternate 320 figure seen cited elsewhere'): the new-gain step is measured here as taking effect arriving AT ISO 400 (320 is the last low-gain point, 400 the first high-gain point) -- both cited figures were describing the same transition from opposite sides of it.

The a6300 and a6500 same-family cross-checks land on the identical ISO 318 -> 400 transition (with slightly different absolute read-noise values), consistent with data/sensors.json's premise that all three share one sensor generation.

Full well varies a little across the three siblings on this chart (a6400 36,443 e-, a6300 38,355 e-, a6500 38,207 e-) -- within normal unit-to-unit/measurement variation for what is reported to be the same silicon, not a evidence of a different chip.

crossCheck_emIII.note: data/sensors.json's existing OM-1 record leaned on a blocked-page search summary (low confidence) for its full-well and DCG-switch figures, using the E-M1 Mark III as a stand-in. This pass loaded photonstophotos.net directly and found the OM-1 itself as its own RN_e.htm/PDR.htm series ('Olympus System OM-1_12') -- see the top-level entry above, which is now a direct reading, not a stand-in. The E-M1 III figures below are kept only as an explicit same-lineage comparison, confirming the two curves really are close except where the OM-1 gains its extra dual-conversion-gain step, matching the DPReview-forum claim data/sensors.json already recorded (low-confidence there; now visually/numerically corroborated here).

dcgIsoCandidate.calc: slope -1.27 stops/stop -- markedly gentler than the OM-1's own -1.94 stops/stop step, i.e. the E-M1 III's curve has no comparably sharp cliff; this candidate is a soft knee, not read as a real second conversion-gain region. See meta.dcgDetectionMethod.

notes: OM-1 full well (19,491 e-) is somewhat lower than the E-M1 III's (21,320 e-, the figure data/sensors.json currently uses as an OM-1 stand-in) -- now that the OM-1 has its own direct chart reading, its own number should replace the stand-in in data/sensors.json.

DCG-switch candidate ISO 800 -> 1006 (essentially ISO 800 -> 1000) matches the existing low-confidence DPReview-forum-derived claim in research/sensor-sources.md ('the OM-1 sensor shows some advantage due to the dual-gain at ISO1000') -- now confirmed directly from the primary chart rather than a blocked-page search summary.

The E-M1 III's own curve (cross-check above) has no comparably sharp cliff anywhere in its normal analog range -- consistent with the existing research note that the OM-1's dual-conversion-gain step is a difference from its predecessor, not a shared feature.

No Sensor_Characteristics.htm (DxOMark-derived) row exists for either the OM-1 or the E-M1 III -- DxOMark has not tested either camera -- so no dxomarkDerived cross-check is available for this pick, unlike the full-frame and APS-C ones.
